region.text: the Pamplona basin and the Basque valleys

ledger.note: 824: Íñigo Arista becomes ruler of Pamplona. 'In an event traditionally dated to 824' Íñigo Arista was elected or declared ruler; infobox 'Established: 824'. The Franks had 'in 806 took Navarre under their protection'.
844: Galindo Aznárez I of Aragon becomes Íñigo's vassal. 'In 844, Aznar's son Galindo was forced to make himself a vassal of Íñigo.'
914: Sancho takes Arnedo. 'Sancho takes Arnedo and attacks Calahorra.'
922: the vassalage ends in absorption. The county 'was incorporated within the crown of Navarre'.

ledger.note: 922: the county of Aragon is absorbed. 'From the death of Galindo Aznárez II, the county of Aragon was incorporated within the crown of Navarre ... into which it was absorbed in 922.'

region.text: the regions of Nájera and Calahorra

ledger.note: 923: Viguera and Nájera fall. The Banu Qasi page: 'Viguera and Nájera fall'; the Navarre page gives Sancho Garcés (905-925) 'the regions of Nájera and Calahorra', undated. The year is the Banu Qasi page's.

region.text: Calahorra and the valley of the River Cidacos

ledger.note: 966: Calahorra is lost. 'In 966, clashes between the Caliphate of Córdoba and the kingdom resulted in the loss of Calahorra and the valley of the River Cidacos.'

1015: Sancho III begins to expand into Sobrarbe. 'In 1015 he began a policy of expansion', displacing Muslim control in the depopulated former county of Sobrarbe; 'later added the counties of Sobrarbe (1015), Ribagorza (1018) and Cea (1030)'. The Muslim power is read as the Taifa of Zaragoza.

ledger.note: 1017: Sancho becomes protector of Castile. 'In 1017, he became the protector of Castile for the young García Sánchez'; 1016 'fixed the border between Navarre and Castile'.

union.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana

ledger.note: 1018: Ribagorza passes to Sancho III. 'In 1018, William Isarn tried to solidify his control over the Arán valley, but was killed. Sancho then took his portion.' (Ribagorza page: 1018-1035 Sancho 'ruled first William Isarn's portion, then the entire county by conquest and submission'.)

union.text: Ribagorza: the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena and Noguera Ribagorzana

ledger.note: 1025: the rival claim to Ribagorza ends. 'Finally resolved in 1025 when Mayor retired to a Castilian convent', leaving the whole county to Sancho.

1028: Count García Sánchez of Castile is assassinated. 'The assassination of Count García Sánchez of Castile in 1028 let Sancho appoint Ferdinand as count' (the Sancho III page says 1027 and Ferdinand's appointment 1029).

region.text: Castile: Burgos, Soria, Cantabria and La Bureba

ledger.note: 1028: Sancho III occupies Castile. Ferdinand is named count; Castile (Burgos, Soria, Cantabria) is drawn inside the kingdom as Cliopatria's 1028 shape does.

1028: Sancho takes the Pisuerga and the Cea from León. 'He seized the country of the Pisuerga and the Cea, which belonged to the Kingdom of León' (the Sancho III page dates the county of Cea to 1030).

region.text: the Duchy of Gascony up to the Garonne

ledger.note: 1032: Sancho extends his authority into Gascony. 'After Sancho VI's death in 1032, Sancho the Great extended his authority definitively into Gascony', claiming up to the Garonne; a protectorate over the Duchy.

region.text: Zamora and the west of León

ledger.note: 1033: Sancho is king 'from Zamora to the borders of Barcelona'. 'By March 1033, he was king from Zamora to the borders of Barcelona.'

region.text: the city of León and the rest of the western kingdom (Salamanca, Valladolid, Palencia, Asturias)

ledger.note: 1034: León falls and Sancho is crowned again. 'In 1034, even the city of León ... fell, and there Sancho had himself crowned again.'

region.text: Sancho III's empire at his death

ledger.note: 1035: Sancho III divides his realm among his four sons. 'Before his death in 1035, Sancho divided his possessions among his sons': García the kingdom of Pamplona, Ferdinand Castile, Gonzalo Sobrarbe and Ribagorza, Ramiro lands in Aragon.
1035: Ferdinand takes Castile and the Pisuerga-Cea. Ferdinand got 'the rest of the County of Castile and the lands between the Pisuerga and the Cea'; García kept the north-east of Castile and Álava.

1035: the western conquests (León, Zamora, Salamanca) leave the kingdom. The pages opened do not say who held them after Sancho's death; they are returned to León, which Ferdinand unites with Castile after 1037.
1035: the Gascon protectorate lapses with Sancho's death. The pages do not say; García inherits 'the Basque lands'.

ledger.note: 1035: Gonzalo takes Sobrarbe and Ribagorza. Gonzalo got 'the counties of Sobrarbe and Ribargoza'; Ribagorza page: he ruled 1035-1045 'as regulus or rex of Ribagorza and Sobrarbe'.

1035: Ramiro gets lands in Aragon. 'Ramiro: given property in the former county of Aragón' (Sancho III page); the Navarre page says García's share 'included ... parts of Aragon', so the split of the county is a reading.

ledger.note: 1035: Gonzalo holds Sobrarbe and Ribagorza 'as vassal of his eldest brother, García'.

ledger.note: 1045: Gonzalo dies and Ramiro absorbs Ribagorza. 'Upon Gonzalo's death: the county was absorbed into the territories of his brother Ramiro I of Aragon.'

ledger.note: 1045: Calahorra is wrested from the Moors. 'Calahorra was wrested from the Moors' (1045; the page also has 'the capture of Calahorra in 1044').

region.text: La Bureba and the Tirón valley

ledger.note: 1054: Atapuerca. Ferdinand 'took from Pamplona the lands in La Bureba and the Tirón River'; García Sánchez III is killed.

region.text: La Rioja, Biscay, Álava, Durango and part of Gipuzkoa

ledger.note: 1076: Alfonso VI takes La Rioja, Biscay, Álava, Durango and part of Gipuzkoa. After the murder of Sancho IV on 4 June 1076 Alfonso VI 'took control of La Rioja, the Lordship of Biscay, the County of Álava, the County of Durango and part of Gipuzkoa'.
1076: Sancho Ramírez takes the rest. Sancho Ramírez of Aragon 'took control of the rest of the territory'; Aragon's core was 'recognised by Alfonso VI as a vassal state'.
1076: the Kingdom of Pamplona is partitioned between Castile and Aragon. 'The murder is dated to 4 June 1076', the year of the split; the kingdom is restored only in 1134.

wars.name: Rebellion of Íñigo Arista with Musa ibn Musa
wars.outcome: 'In 841, in concert with Musa ibn Musa, Íñigo rebelled' (Navarre page); the Banu Qasi page has Abd ar-Rahman II defeat them and take Musa's son Lubb hostage. No border moved.
wars.note: Íñigo was 'still in rebellion at the time of his death in 851/2'.

zones.text: Albelda and Monte Laturce in La Rioja

wars.outcome: 'In 859, Ordoño I of Asturias and García Íñiguez of Pamplona joined forces to deal Musa a crushing defeat.' No land recorded as taken.

wars.name: Cordoban campaigns of 920 and 924 against Pamplona
wars.outcome: Abd al-Rahman III beat Navarre and León at Valdejunquera on 26 July 920 and sacked Pamplona; in 924 he devastated Basque territory in a counter-offensive against Sancho Ordóñez of Navarre. No lasting loss recorded.
wars.note: The Navarre page gives Valdejunquera no year and dates the attack on Pamplona to 'by 924'.

wars.outcome: Sobrarbe (1015), Ribagorza (1018, 1025), Castile (1028; 1027 on the Sancho III page), the Pisuerga-Cea (1028 or 1030), Zamora (March 1033) and León (1034); at his death in 1035 'the kingdom had reached its greatest historical extent'.

wars.name: Partition of Pamplona after the murder of Sancho IV

zones.text: La Rioja, Biscay, Álava, Durango and part of Gipuzkoa

wars.outcome: Alfonso VI of León and Castile takes La Rioja, Biscay, Álava, Durango and part of Gipuzkoa; Sancho Ramírez of Aragon takes the rest. Part of the Basque lands 'went back to the Pamplonese kingdom' by the Peace of Támara in 1127, and the kingdom is restored in 1134.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary lines. The border with Castile was 'fixed' by Sancho III in 1016 (Sancho III page) and is the one sharper frontier; the Ebro frontier with the Muslim marches, the Pyrenean counties and the Basque west are approximate.

notes: One kingdom or two: Wikipedia has a single article (infobox 'Originally the Kingdom of Pamplona; later the Kingdom of Navarre', 824-1841) and Cliopatria gives both rows Wikidata Q200262. This dossier takes the kingdom to 1076, when it was partitioned between Castile and Aragon after the murder of Sancho IV; it was restored in 1134 (Navarre page), and the Kingdom of Navarre dossier of another group continues it from Cliopatria's 1139 row. The reviewer may merge the two; the Navarre rows (1139-1428) are not reviewed here, outside the 1-2 page budget. Cliopatria's 'County of Ribagorza' row (866-1084) is mostly this kingdom: the 866-874 shape is the Pamplona 860 shape cell for cell, the 875-1027 shapes add 23-28 cells of Sobrarbe and Ribagorza, 1028-1039 are Sancho III's empire (with 73 Catalan cells that no page supports), 1040-1084 are García III's and Sancho IV's Navarre. The new keyframes kingdom-of-pamplona_866 to _1054 replace those shapes; the county-of-ribagorza dossier marks the same shapes wrong. Not settled: the kings between 931 and 970 and between 994 and 1004; the border of 9th-century Pamplona (the Navarre page gives only the 905 extent 'to Nájera and Arba'); the alliance with Córdoba under Fortún Garcés (882-905), the 934 vassalage of Queen Toda to Abd al-Rahman III (Abd al-Rahman III page: 'made Queen Toda submit as a vassal'; this belongs in the caliphate-of-cordoba ledger); the status of Viguera (970-994). Page conflicts: Castile occupied in 1027 (Sancho III page) or 1028 (Navarre page); the county of Cea 1028 or 1030; Calahorra 1044 or 1045. Counterparts: banu-qasi is written by eu-12-a; still needing a dossier: Castile before Cliopatria's 961 row (the County of Castile page: first wider count Rodrigo 850, Fernán González 931, García Sánchez killed 1028), carried here under the kingdom-of-castile slug; the county-of-ribagorza dossier is written here. Names needed in the gazetteer: Sobrarbe, Ribagorza, Nájera, Calahorra, Viguera, La Bureba, the Pisuerga and Cea valleys.
